title: The Second Edge Theorem: The Asymptotic Collapse of Sample-Dependent Information Geometry to the Canonical Flat Canvas of Conventional Statistics in Large Sample Limits

paper.title: The Second Edge Theorem: The Asymptotic Collapse of Sample-Dependent Information Geometry to the Canonical Flat Canvas of Conventional Statistics in Large Sample Limits
paper.abstract: Abstract This paper establishes the complete global proof of the Second Edge Theorem , proving that as the sample size grows to infinity, the sequence of curved, sample-dependent joint information-geometric manifolds—formulated by the parameter space, sample-scaled Fisher metric, and dual alpha-connections—undergoes an asymptotic phase transition, metric-topological shrinkage, and global geometric collapse onto the flat canonical tangent canvas of Conventional Statistics defined by the tangent space at the true parameter, the base Fisher metric, and the zero-curvature Levi-Civita connection. First, we discover and prove the universal tensor valence scaling law, which dictates that tensor fields across valences one through four degenerate according to the sample size raised to the power of one minus half the valence. Under this unified scaling law, score one-form fluctuations stabilize to a normalized Gaussian field, the sample-scaled Fisher metric freezes uniformly to the constant single-observation Fisher metric at the true parameter, Amari affine connections dissolve at an inverse square-root sample rate to zero Christoffel symbols, and intrinsic Riemann curvature undergoes accelerated annihilation down to identical zero at an inverse sample rate. Second, we resolve the long-standing geometric-operational duality by bridging differential-geometric manifold collapse with statistical decision theory. Through the formulation of the Taylor-Geometry Algebraic Functional Identity and the Double Completeness Architecture, we prove that Cheeger-Gromov spatial manifold flattening and Le Cam decision risk condensation are mathematically non-separable dual projections of the exact same underlying asymptotic phase transition. Third, by constructing a Fisher-Compatible Ehresmann Connection over the statistical fiber bundle, we extend the theory to over-parameterized and singular models without requiring ambient metric non-degeneracy. On the non-singular horizontal distribution, we demonstrate Gromov-Hausdorff leaf space collapse, accelerated annihilation of the restricted holonomy group diameter, and global uniformization of local asymptotic normality under the Le Cam deficiency distance. Fourth, by unifying the First Edge Theorem and the Second Edge Theorem, we establish the nested dual-edge hierarchy of statistical science, demonstrating that Conventional Statistics forms the boundary of Information Geometry, which itself forms the boundary of Statistical Mechanics and Geometry. This proves that Conventional Statistics is not a heuristic approximation, but the unique, zero-curvature thermodynamic attractor state toward which all regular parametric information manifolds dynamically collapse in the infinite-sample limit. Finally, by extending our horizon to Statistically Meaningful Geometry (SMG), modern statistics transcends its classical role as a static theory of flat asymptotic inference. When formulated within the full SMG framework, modern statistics evolves into a dynamic, non-equilibrium field theory capable of explicitly modeling finite-sample fluctuations, phase transitions, topological structures, over-parametrization models, and gauge-invariant interactions—redefining statistical inference as the active, thermodynamic geometry of complex systems rather than a passive infinite-sample limit.

sections.heading: 1.1 Motivations, Backgrounds, and Architectural Targets
sections.text: Classical large-sample statistical theory implicitly operates under the foundational premise that as sample size N → ∞ N\to\infty , estimation, inference, and decision testing occur within a linear, flat Euclidean workspace. However, finite-sample statistical parametric families are intrinsically curved Riemannian-affine manifolds [ 4 , 41 ] . Historical literature frequently treats the transition from curved finite-sample models to flat asymptotic limit experiments as an ad-hoc analytic convenience or a passive collection of scalar point limits [ 17 , 50 ] . To eliminate circular reasoning, topological ambiguities, and informal coordinate heuristics, this section constructs a rigorous axiomatic baseline. We define the ambient statistical universe, establish the natural linear vector space derivation isomorphism between differential tangent spaces and arithmetic coordinates, formalize the Triadic Variable Spectrum, and establish the Epistemological Equivalence Theorem proving that General Conventional Statistics ( CS ) is mathematically equivalent to the canonical flat tangent space ℳ ∞ \mathcal{M}_{\infty} .

sections.heading: 5.1.3 The Ehresmann Connection Instrument as the Geometric Solution
sections.text: To resolve this failure without abandoning over-parameterized models, we introduce the Ehresmann Connection Instrument . Instead of treating Θ \Theta as an unstructured ambient manifold ℝ D \mathbb{R}^{D} , we equip it with a fiber bundle structure ( Θ , ℬ , π ) (\Theta,\mathcal{B},\pi) where: • The base manifold ℬ ≡ Θ / ∼ \mathcal{B}\equiv\Theta/\sim represents the d d -dimensional quotient space of observationally identifiable probability distributions, where g ℬ g^{\mathcal{B}} is strictly non-singular ( λ min ​ ( g ℬ ) ≥ κ 0 > 0 \lambda_{\min}(g^{\mathcal{B}})\geq\kappa_{0}>0 ). • The fiber ℱ p = π − 1 ​ ( p ) \mathcal{F}_{p}=\pi^{-1}(p) represents the ( D − d ) (D-d) -dimensional unidentifiable gauge orbit. 8 8 8 Let ( Θ , ℬ , π ) (\Theta,\mathcal{B},\pi) be a statistical fiber bundle, where π : Θ → ℬ \pi:\Theta\to\mathcal{B} is the canonical projection map from the ambient parameter space Θ ⊂ ℝ D \Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^{D} to the quotient base manifold ℬ ≡ Θ / ∼ \mathcal{B}\equiv\Theta/\sim of identifiable probability distributions. For any point p ∈ ℬ p\in\mathcal{B} , the fiber (or preimage) π − 1 ​ ( p ) ⊂ Θ \pi^{-1}(p)\subset\Theta over p p is defined as: π − 1 ( p ) ≡ { θ ∈ Θ : π ( θ ) = p } = { θ ∈ Θ : P θ = p μ -a.e. } \pi^{-1}(p)\equiv\left\{\theta\in\Theta:\pi(\theta)=p\right\}=\left\{\theta\in\Theta:P_{\theta}=p\quad\mu\text{-a.e.}\right\} (183) More generally, as a set-valued map π − 1 : 𝒫 ⁡ ( ℬ ) → 𝒫 ⁡ ( Θ ) \pi^{-1}:\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{B})\to\mathcal{P}(\Theta) on the power set of ℬ \mathcal{B} , the inverse image map for any subset 𝒰 ⊆ ℬ \mathcal{U}\subseteq\mathcal{B} is defined as: π − 1 ​ ( 𝒰 ) ≡ { θ ∈ Θ : π ⁡ ( θ ) ∈ 𝒰 } = ⋃ p ∈ 𝒰 π − 1 ​ ( p ) \pi^{-1}(\mathcal{U})\equiv\left\{\theta\in\Theta:\pi(\theta)\in\mathcal{U}\right\}=\bigcup_{p\in\mathcal{U}}\pi^{-1}(p) (184) The Ehresmann connection provides a smooth, canonically invariant decomposition of the ambient tangent space into vertical and horizontal sub-bundles: T θ Θ = H θ ⊕ V θ , where V θ ≡ ker ( d π θ ) and H θ ≡ V θ ⟂ g . T_{\theta}\Theta=H_{\theta}\oplus V_{\theta},\quad\text{where }V_{\theta}\equiv\ker(d\pi_{\theta})\text{ and }H_{\theta}\equiv V_{\theta}^{\perp_{g}}. (185) By projecting localized coordinate charts and operators onto the horizontal distribution H θ H_{\theta} via the projection operator P θ H ≡ id T θ ​ Θ − ω θ P_{\theta}^{H}\equiv\mathrm{id}_{T_{\theta}\Theta}-\omega_{\theta} , we isolate the non-identifiable gauge modes in V θ V_{\theta} while preserving a strictly positive-definite restricted metric g θ | H θ × H θ g_{\theta}\big|_{H_{\theta}\times H_{\theta}} . Let Θ ⊂ ℝ D \Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^{D} be a smooth, open, D D -dimensional ambient parameter space, and let 𝒫 = { P θ : d P θ = p ( x ; θ ) d μ ( x ) , θ ∈ Θ } \mathcal{P}=\{P_{\theta}:dP_{\theta}=p(x;\theta)d\mu(x),\,\theta\in\Theta\} be a dominated parametric family on sample space 𝒳 \mathcal{X} . sections.heading: Step 4: Uniform Lower Bound via Compact Sphere Isolation.
sections.text: To transition from point-wise strict positive-definiteness to a uniform lower bound on the minimum eigenvalue across the entire localized neighborhood 𝒰 ⁡ ( θ 0 ) ⊂ Θ \mathcal{U}(\theta_{0})\subset\Theta , we formalize the proof through four transparent logical phases.

sections.heading: Phase 1: Compact Domain Construction.
sections.text: Let 𝒰 ¯ ​ ( θ 0 ) ⊂ Θ \overline{\mathcal{U}}(\theta_{0})\subset\Theta denote the closed, bounded neighborhood (compact closure) of θ 0 \theta_{0} in the ambient space ℝ D \mathbb{R}^{D} . Let H θ 0 ≅ ℝ d H_{\theta_{0}}\cong\mathbb{R}^{d} be the d d -dimensional horizontal subspace at state θ 0 \theta_{0} . (208) By the Heine-Borel Theorem [ 45 ] , 𝒰 ¯ ​ ( θ 0 ) \overline{\mathcal{U}}(\theta_{0}) is closed and bounded in ℝ D \mathbb{R}^{D} , hence compact. Similarly, 𝕊 d − 1 \mathbb{S}^{d-1} is closed and bounded in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} , hence compact [ 45 ] . By Tychonoff’s Theorem on product topologies [ 36 ] , the Cartesian product space: K ≡ 𝒰 ¯ ​ ( θ 0 ) × 𝕊 d − 1 ⊂ ℝ D × ℝ d K\equiv\overline{\mathcal{U}}(\theta_{0})\times\mathbb{S}^{d-1}\subset\mathbb{R}^{D}\times\mathbb{R}^{d} (209) is a non-empty, compact topological space.

sections.heading: 6 The Geometric-Operational Unification Theorem Without Ambient Non-Degeneracy
sections.text: In Section 5 , we constructed the Fisher-compatible Ehresmann connection framework over the statistical fiber bundle ( Θ , ℬ , π ) (\Theta,\mathcal{B},\pi) , decomposing the tangent bundle into mutually metric-orthogonal sub-bundles T θ ​ Θ = H θ ⊕ V θ T_{\theta}\Theta=H_{\theta}\oplus V_{\theta} . By isolating the structural internal directions V θ = ker ⁡ ( d ​ π θ ) V_{\theta}=\ker(d\pi_{\theta}) from the statistically verifiable directions H θ = V θ ⟂ g H_{\theta}=V_{\theta}^{\perp_{g}} , Theorem 9 established that the restricted Fisher metric g θ | H θ × H θ g_{\theta}\big|_{H_{\theta}\times H_{\theta}} is strictly positive-definite and non-singular ( λ min ​ ( g θ | H θ ) ≥ κ 0 > 0 \lambda_{\min}(g_{\theta}|_{H_{\theta}})\geq\kappa_{0}>0 ), even when the ambient metric g θ g_{\theta} exhibits massive degeneracies due to over-parameterization. In this section, we present the formal proof of the Geometric-Operational Unification Theorem restricted to the horizontal distribution H θ H_{\theta} (and the quotient base manifold ℬ \mathcal{B} ). We demonstrate that the Geometric Priority Paradigm (Axiom 1 ) and the Statistical Operationalism Paradigm (Axiom 2 ) are mathematically equivalent without requiring ambient parameter space identifiability or non-degeneracy. This establishes the unified bridge between differential geometry and decision theory on the non-singular horizontal carriage.

sections.heading: 6.4 Epistemological Synthesis and Elimination of Non-Identifiability Pathologies
sections.text: The unification established in Section 6 demonstrates that ambient parameter space non-identifiability ( det g ( 1 ) ​ ( θ ) = 0 \det g^{(1)}(\theta)=0 ) does not present an insurmountable barrier to Local Asymptotic Normality (LAN) or information-geometric stability. In high-dimensional, over-parameterized statistical systems—such as deep neural architectures, singular exponential families, and singular latent variable models—the parameter space Θ ⊆ ℝ D \Theta\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{D} ( D ≫ d D\gg d ) possesses continuous gauge symmetries. Under these symmetries, infinitely many parameter vectors θ ∈ Θ \theta\in\Theta yield identical observational probability distributions P θ ∈ ℬ P_{\theta}\in\mathcal{B} . By introducing the Fisher-Compatible Ehresmann Connection ( ω θ \omega_{\theta} ), the ambient tangent bundle decomposes into two mutually orthogonal sub-bundles: T θ Θ = H θ ⊕ V θ , where V θ ≡ ker ( d π θ ) and H θ ≡ V θ ⟂ g . T_{\theta}\Theta=H_{\theta}\oplus V_{\theta},\quad\text{where }V_{\theta}\equiv\ker(d\pi_{\theta})\text{ and }H_{\theta}\equiv V_{\theta}^{\perp_{g}}. (284) This horizontal-vertical splitting acts as a geometric filter: (i) Vertical Sub-bundle ( V θ V_{\theta} ): Absorbs all unidentifiable gauge directions, internal parameter redundancies, and zero-eigenvalue modes of the Fisher information matrix. (ii) Horizontal Sub-bundle ( H θ H_{\theta} ): Isolates the statistically verifiable, information-carrying directions that map bijectively onto the d d -dimensional quotient base manifold ℬ ≡ Θ / ∼ \mathcal{B}\equiv\Theta/\sim of identifiable probability distributions. By restricting localized experiments and tensor pullbacks strictly to the horizontal distribution H θ 0 ≅ T π ⁡ ( θ 0 ) ​ ℬ H_{\theta_{0}}\cong T_{\pi(\theta_{0})}\mathcal{B} , we eliminate all ambient metric singularities and establish a well-posed, gauge-invariant asymptotic decision framework.

First, we discover and prove the universal tensor valence scaling law, which dictates that tensor fields across valences one through four degenerate according to the sample size raised to the power of one minus half the valence. Under this unified scaling law, score one-form fluctuations stabilize to a normalized Gaussian field, the sample-scaled Fisher metric freezes uniformly to the constant single-observation Fisher metric at the true parameter, Amari affine connections dissolve at an inverse square-root sample rate to zero Christoffel symbols, and intrinsic Riemann curvature undergoes accelerated annihilation down to identical zero at an inverse sample rate. Second, we resolve the long-standing geometric-operational duality by bridging differential-geometric manifold collapse with statistical decision theory. Through the formulation of the Taylor-Geometry Algebraic Functional Identity and the Double Completeness Architecture, we prove that Cheeger-Gromov spatial manifold flattening and Le Cam decision risk condensation are mathematically non-separable dual projections of the exact same underlying asymptotic phase transition. Third, by constructing a Fisher-Compatible Ehresmann Connection over the statistical fiber bundle, we extend the theory to over-parameterized and singular models without requiring ambient metric non-degeneracy. On the non-singular horizontal distribution, we demonstrate Gromov-Hausdorff leaf space collapse, accelerated annihilation of the restricted holonomy group diameter, and global uniformization of local asymptotic normality under the Le Cam deficiency distance. Fourth, by unifying the First Edge Theorem and the Second Edge Theorem, we establish the nested dual-edge hierarchy of statistical science, demonstrating that Conventional Statistics forms the boundary of Information Geometry, which itself forms the boundary of Statistical Mechanics and Geometry. This proves that Conventional Statistics is not a heuristic approximation, but the unique, zero-curvature thermodynamic attractor state toward which all regular parametric information manifolds dynamically collapse in the infinite-sample limit. Finally, by extending our horizon to Statistically Meaningful Geometry (SMG), modern statistics transcends its classical role as a static theory of flat asymptotic inference. When formulated within the full SMG framework, modern statistics evolves into a dynamic, non-equilibrium field theory capable of explicitly modeling finite-sample fluctuations, phase transitions, topological structures, over-parametrization models, and gauge-invariant interactions—redefining statistical inference as the active, thermodynamic geometry of complex systems rather than a passive infinite-sample limit. 1 Epistemological Foundations, Regularity Axioms, and Target Universes 1.1 Motivations, Backgrounds, and Architectural Targets Classical large-sample statistical theory implicitly operates under the foundational premise that as sample size N → ∞ N	o\infty , estimation, inference, and decision testing occur within a linear, flat Euclidean workspace.
